question: The height of stumps in cricket is ______.
solution:
The correct answer is 28 inches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The three vertical pillars that support the bails and create the wicket in cricket are known as the stumps.**
 
• A batsman might be dismissed by getting stumped or by being stumped oneself.
 
• Except for the bail grooves,** the tops of the stumps must be dome-shaped and 28 inches/71.12 **cm above the playing surface.
 
• Apart from the domed top, a stump's **uppermost** component must be **cylindrical** with a **circular section with a diameter of at least 1.38 in (3.50 cm) and no more than 1.5 in (3.81 cm).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information**__

**Stumps**

 
• 
 
 
• **Three vertical posts serve as the stumps and hold up two bails.** At each end of the pitch, a wicket is created by the combination of the stumps and bails, which are typically constructed of wood, most frequently ash.
 
• **Each stump is identified with a unique name:**
 
 
• **Off stump** is the stump that is on the other side of the wicket from the batsman.
 
• **The middle of the three stumps **is referred to as the middle stump.
 
• **Leg stump** is the stump that is on the same side as the batsman's legs as the wicket.
